units.en: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing won favor through flattery, monopolized power, and Zai grew still more distant.
units.literal: It happened that Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing through fawning and favoritism were close and cherished, monopolizing the balance of power, while Zai grew still more distant.

units.zh: 文慶等因共譖縡受高驪使金，後主收縡下獄。
units.en: Wenqing and the others then slandered Zai for taking gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu had him arrested and imprisoned.
units.literal: Wenqing and the others therefore together slandered Zai for receiving gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu arrested Zai and put him in prison.

units.zh: 縡素剛，因憤恚，乃於獄中上書曰：「夫君人者，恭事上帝，子愛下民，省嗜慾，遠諂佞，未明求衣，日旰忘食，是以澤被區宇，慶流子孫。
units.en: Zai was by nature unyielding; in rage he submitted a memorial from prison: "A ruler should respectfully serve Heaven, love the people, curb desire, keep far from flatterers, rise at unclear dawn and forget food at sundown—then grace covers the realm and blessing reaches his heirs.
units.literal: Zai by nature was firm; in indignant rage he thereupon submitted a memorial from prison, saying: "The ruler ought to respectfully serve the Supreme Lord, love and cherish the people below, reduce cravings and desires, keep far from flattery and favoritism, at unclear dawn seek clothing, at sundown forget food—thereby grace covers the realm and blessing flows to sons and grandsons.

units.zh: 陛下頃來酒色過度，不虔郊廟之神，專媚淫昏之鬼；
units.en: Your Majesty of late has gone to excess in wine and sex, neglects the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes only on ghosts of lewd darkness;
units.literal: Your Majesty of late has passed bounds in wine and sex, is not reverent toward the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes on the ghosts of lewd darkness alone;

units.zh: 小人在側，宦豎弄權，惡忠直若仇讎，視生民如草芥；
units.en: petty men stand at your side, eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and upright as enemies, and treat the people like grass;
units.literal: petty men are at your side, palace eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and straight as enemies, and regard living people as grass and stubble;

units.zh: 後宮曳綺繡，廄馬餘菽粟，百姓流離，殭尸蔽野；
units.en: the rear palace trails brocade while stable horses leave grain unused, the people wander homeless, and stiff corpses cover the wilds;
units.literal: in the rear palace trailing brocade and embroidery, in the stables horses leave grain and millet surplus, while the people wander displaced and stiff corpses cover the wilds;

units.zh: 貨賄公行，帑藏損耗，神怒民怨，眾叛親離。
units.en: bribes run openly, the treasury drains, spirits rage and the people resent, the masses rebel and kin turn away.
units.literal: bribes go openly, the treasury is drained, the spirits are angry and the people resentful, the masses rebel and kin turn away.

units.zh: 恐東南王氣，自斯而盡。」
units.en: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends here."
units.literal: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends from this."

units.zh: 書奏，後主大怒。
units.en: When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged.

units.zh: 頃之，意稍解，遣使謂縡曰：「我欲赦卿，卿能改過不？」
units.en: Before long his anger cooled somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai, "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?"
units.literal: Before long his mind eased somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?"

units.zh: 縡對曰：「臣心如面，臣面可改，則臣心可改。」
units.en: Zai replied, "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change."
units.literal: Zai replied: "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change."

units.zh: 後主於是益怒，令宦者李善慶窮治其事，[7]遂賜死獄中，時年五十五。
units.en: Houzhu then grew still angrier and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate to the end, [7] and Zai was ordered to die in prison, aged fifty-five.
units.literal: Houzhu thereupon grew still more angry and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate the matter to the end, [7] and Zai was granted death in prison, aged fifty-five.

units.zh: 有集十卷行於世。
units.en: A collection of writings in ten scrolls circulated after his death.
units.literal: He had a collection of writings in ten scrolls circulating in the world.

units.zh: 時有吳興章華，字仲宗，家世農夫，至華獨好學，與士君子遊處，頗覽經史，善屬文。
units.en: At the time Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong, came from a farming family—he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, read widely in the classics and histories, and wrote well.
units.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.

units.zh: 侯景之亂，乃遊嶺南，居羅浮山寺，專精習業。
units.en: During Hou Jing's turmoil he fled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.
units.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing he then traveled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.

units.zh: 歐陽頠為廣州刺史，署為南海太守。
units.en: Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, appointed him administrator of Nanhai.
units.literal: Ouyang Wei was inspector of Guangzhou and appointed him Administrator of Nanhai.

units.zh: 及歐陽紇敗，乃還京師。
units.en: When Ouyang He was defeated he returned to the capital.
units.literal: When Ouyang He was defeated he then returned to the capital.

units.zh: 太建中，高宗使吏部侍郎蕭引喻廣州刺史馬靖，令入子為質，引奏華與俱行。
units.en: In the Taijian era, Emperor Xuan sent vice minister of personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany the mission.
units.literal: In the Taijian era, Emperor Xuan sent vice minister of personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send in his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany him.

units.zh: 使還，而高宗崩。
units.en: When the mission returned, Emperor Xuan had died.
units.literal: When the mission returned, Emperor Xuan had died.

units.zh: 後主即位，朝臣以華素無伐閱，競排詆之，乃除大市令，既雅非所好，乃辭以疾，鬱鬱不得志。
units.en: When Houzhu took the throne, court gentlemen—Hua had no record of merit—competed to slander him; he was made director of the great market. That post ill suited him; he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and thwarted.
units.literal: When Houzhu took the throne the court gentlemen, because Hua by nature had no meritorious background, all competed to slander him; he was therefore made director of the great market. As it was utterly not to his liking, he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and without achieving his aim.

units.zh: 禎明初，上書極諫，其大略曰：「昔高祖南平百越，北誅逆虜；
units.en: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, saying in gist: "In the past the Founder pacified the Hundred Yue in the south and punished the rebel captives in the north;
units.literal: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of extreme remonstrance; its general purport said: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebellious captives;

units.zh: 世祖東定吳會，西破王琳；
units.en: Emperor Wen eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;
units.literal: Emperor Wen eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;

units.zh: 高宗克復淮南，辟地千里：三祖之功，亦至勤矣。
units.en: Emperor Xuan recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was utmost diligence.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was also utmost diligence.

units.zh: 陛下即位，于今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏，溺於嬖寵，惑於酒色，祠七廟而不出，拜妃嬪而臨軒，老臣宿將，棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪，昇之朝廷。
units.en: Your Majesty has reigned five years without remembering the former emperor's hardships or fearing Heaven's mandate, drowning in favorites and delusion of wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, casting old ministers and veteran generals to the wilds and raising flatterers and slanderers.
units.literal: Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not thinking of the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared, drowning in favorites, deluded by wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, old ministers and veteran generals cast to the wild grass, flatterers and slanderous villains raised into the court.

units.zh: 今疆埸日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改絃易張，臣見麋鹿復遊於姑蘇臺矣。」
units.en: Now the frontier shrinks daily and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change course, I see deer roaming the Gusu Terrace again."
units.literal: Now the frontier daily narrows and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change the string and ease the bow, I see deer again roaming the Gusu Terrace."

units.zh: 書奏，後主大怒，即日命斬之。
units.en: When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious and ordered him beheaded that same day.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged and that same day ordered him beheaded.

units.zh: 史臣曰：蕭濟、陸瓊，俱以才學顯著，顧野王博極群典，傅縡聰警特達，並一代之英靈矣。
units.en: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both shone for talent and learning; Gu Yewang mastered the canon; Fu Zai was brilliantly sharp—all spirits of an age.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both for talent and learning were illustrious; Gu Yewang's learning exhausted the canon; Fu Zai was sharp-witted and outstanding—all spirits of an age.

units.zh: 然縡不能循道進退，遂寘極網，悲夫！
units.en: Yet Zai could not advance and withdraw by the Way and so fell into the utmost net—pitiable!
units.literal: Yet Zai could not follow the Way in advancing and withdrawing and therefore fell into the utmost net—pitiable!

units.zh: 武陵王舉兵至峽口，王琳偏將陸納等據湘州應之，沖為納所拘。
units.en: When the Prince of Wuling marched to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others seized Xiangzhou in support; Chong was held by Na.
units.literal: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others held Xiangzhou in response; Chong was detained by Na.

units.zh: 梁世為國子周易生，射策舉高第，除祕書郎、太子舍人、宣惠武陵王主簿、輕車河東王功曹史。
units.en: Under Liang he studied the Book of Changes at the national university, took top marks in the archery-and-writing examination, and served as secretary, mentor to the heir apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and records officer to the Prince of Hedong.
units.literal: In Liang he was a National University student in the Book of Changes, scored highest in the archery-and-writing examination, appointed Secretary, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and Records Officer to the Prince of Hedong.

units.zh: 憲時年十四，被召為國子正言生，謁祭酒到溉，溉目而送之，愛其神彩。
units.en: Xian was fourteen when he was made a Correct Sayings student at the National University. He visited libationer Dao Gai, who watched him leave and admired his bearing.
units.literal: Xian was then fourteen and was summoned as a Correct Sayings student of the National University; he called on the libationer Dao Gai, who watched him departing and admired his spirit and bearing.

units.zh: 大同八年，武帝撰孔子正言章句，詔下國學，宣制旨義。
units.en: In Datong year eight the emperor composed his commentary on the Correct Sayings of Confucius and ordered the National University to expound the imperial interpretation.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Datong the Emperor composed section-and-clause commentary on the Correct Sayings of Confucius and ordered it sent down to the National University to proclaim the imperial meaning.

units.zh: 江南渠帥熊曇朗、周迪懷貳，琳遣李孝欽、樊猛與余孝頃同討之。
units.en: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.
units.literal: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.

units.zh: 三將軍敗，並為敵所囚。
units.en: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.
units.literal: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.

units.zh: 于時濟陽江總、吳國顧野王、陸瓊、從弟瑜、河南褚玠、北地傅縡等，皆以才學之美，晨夕娛侍。
units.en: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Jie of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others, all famed for learning, served the heir morning and evening as literary companions.
units.literal: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Jie of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others, all distinguished for literary talent, served morning and evening as companions.

units.zh: 時尚書右丞徐祚、尚書左丞沈客卿俱來候貞，見其形體骨立，祚等愴然歎息，徐喻之曰：「弟年事已衰，禮有恆制，小宜引割自全。」
units.en: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him, "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."
units.literal: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him: "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."

units.zh: 客卿曰：「謝公家傳至孝，士大夫誰不仰止，此恐不能起，如何？」
units.en: Keqing said, "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"
units.literal: Keqing said: "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"

units.zh: 至德三年，以母憂去職。
units.en: In Zhide year 3 (585) he left office on his mother's mourning.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhide he left office on his mother's mourning.

units.zh: 祚謂客卿曰：「信哉，孝門有孝子。」
units.en: Xu said to Keqing, "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."
units.literal: Xu said to Keqing: "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."

units.zh: 後主因敕舍人施文慶曰[2]：「謝貞在王處，未有祿秩，可賜米百石。」
units.en: Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Shi Wenqing [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
units.literal: Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Shi Wenqing, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."

units.zh: 後主因敕舍人施文慶曰 「慶」原本訛「憂」，各本不訛，今改正。
units.en: On "Houzhu thereupon charged palace attendant Shi Wenqing": the base text wrongly wrote you for qing in Wenqing; other editions are correct; now emended.
units.literal: Houzhu thereupon charged palace attendant Shi Wenqing, saying: the character "qing" in the base text was wrongly written "you"; other editions are not in error; now corrected.

units.zh: 孫瑒字德璉，吳郡吳人也。
units.en: Sun Yang, styled Delian, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Sun Yang, styled Delian, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 瑒少倜儻，好謀略，博涉經史，尤便書翰。
units.en: As a youth Yang was bold and fond of strategy; he read widely in the classics and histories and excelled at correspondence.
units.literal: Yang in youth was free and bold, loved strategy, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially skilled at letters.

units.zh: 後主臨哭盡哀，贈護軍將軍，侍中如故，給鼓吹一部，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事量加資給，諡曰桓子。
units.en: The Last Emperor came in person to mourn with deepest grief. He was posthumously made general who guards the army, palace attendant as before, with pipes and drums, court robes, and a suit of garments; funeral costs were generously supplied; his posthumous title was Huanzi.
units.literal: The Last Emperor came in person to mourn and wept with utmost grief; posthumously he was given General Who Guards the Army, palace attendant as before, one set of martial pipes and drums, one set of court robes, one suit of garments; funeral rites were supplied in generous measure according to the occasion; his posthumous title was Huanzi.

units.zh: 瑒從大軍沿流而下，及克姑熟，瑒力戰有功，除員外散騎常侍，封富陽縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: He followed the main fleet downstream. At the taking of Guni he fought with distinction and was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and Marquis of Fuyang with one thousand households.
units.literal: Yang followed the great army downriver; when Guni was taken Yang fought hard with merit; he was removed and made Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang county with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 天嘉元年，授使持節、散騎常侍、安南將軍、湘州刺史，封定襄縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 太清之難，授假節、宣猛將軍、軍主。
units.en: In the Taiqing turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
units.literal: In the turmoil of Taiqing he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.

units.zh: 及吳明徹軍敗呂梁，授使持節、督緣江水陸諸軍事、鎮西將軍，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: When Wu Mingche was broken at Lüliang he was made bearer of the staff, commander of frontier river and land forces, general who guards the west, with a suite of pipes and drums.
units.literal: When Wu Mingche's army was defeated at Lüliang he was given Bearer of the Staff and command of river and land forces along the frontier, made General Who Guards the West, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊於郢州，徵瑒為太府卿，〔三〕加通直散騎常侍。
units.en: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin enthroned Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou. Yang was summoned as grand steward [3] and promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
units.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Wang Lin set up Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou; Yang was summoned as Grand Steward, and promoted to Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 後主嗣位，復除通直散騎常侍，兼起部尚書。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded he was again made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and concurrent minister for founding works.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded he was again removed and made Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, concurrently Minister for Founding Works.

units.zh: 俄加散騎常侍，遷侍中、祠部尚書。
units.en: Before long he was added scattered-cavalry regular attendant, then made palace attendant and minister of the ancestral temples.
units.literal: Before long he was added Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and transferred to Palace Attendant and Minister of the Ancestral Temples.

units.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，王琳為前軍，琳與瑒同門，乃表薦為戎昭將軍、宜都太守，仍從僧辯救徐文盛於武昌。
units.en: When Wang Sengbian attacked Hou Jing, Wang Lin led the van. Lin and Yang were schoolmates; Lin recommended him as martial-announcements general and administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to relieve Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.
units.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Wang Lin was vanguard; Lin and Yang were of the same gate, and Lin memorialized recommending him as Martial-Announcements General and Administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to rescue Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.

units.zh: 仍改授持節、安東將軍、吳郡太守，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was then made bearer of the staff, pacifying-the-east general, and administrator of Wu commandery, with a suite of martial pipes and drums.
units.literal: He was thereupon reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Pacifying-the-East General, and Administrator of Wu commandery, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.

units.zh: 太建四年，授都督荊信二州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史，出鎮公安。
units.en: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was made commander of Jing and Xin, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Jing, and marched out to hold Gong'an.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was given command of military affairs in Jing and Xin provinces, made Pacifying-the-West General and Inspector of Jing, and went out to garrison Gong'an.

units.zh: 常於山齋設講肆，集玄儒之士，冬夏資奉，為學者所稱。
units.en: He often held a lecture hall in his mountain retreat, gathered learned men, and supported them winter and summer; scholars praised him for it.
units.literal: He often set up a lecture hall in his mountain studio, gathered scholars of the profound learning, and supported them winter and summer; scholars praised him.

units.zh: 世子讓，早卒。
units.en: The heir Rang died young.
units.literal: The heir Rang died young.

units.zh: 第二子訓，頗知名，歷臨湘令，直閤將軍、高唐太守。
units.en: The second son Xun won some fame as magistrate of Linxiang, direct-gate general, and administrator of Gaotang.
units.literal: The second son Xun was rather famed; he served in succession as magistrate of Linxiang, Direct-Gate General, and Administrator of Gaotang.

units.zh: 瑒二十一子，咸有父風。
units.en: Yang had twenty-one sons, each with his father's bearing.
units.literal: Yang had twenty-one sons; all had their father's manner.

units.zh: 瑒事親以孝聞，於諸弟甚篤睦。
units.en: Yang was known for filial service to his parents and deep affection for his younger brothers.
units.literal: Yang served his parents with filial fame and was deeply affectionate toward his younger brothers.

units.zh: 有鑒識，男女婚姻，皆擇素貴。
units.en: He had a keen eye; for his children's marriages he always chose families of quiet distinction.
units.literal: He had discernment; in marriages for sons and daughters he always chose families of plain nobility.

units.zh: 起家梁輕車臨川嗣王行參軍，累遷為安西邵陵王水曹中兵參軍事。
units.en: He entered service as acting aide to Liang's Heir of Linchuan in the light-chariot office, then rose to water-and-arms clerk on the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, pacifier of the west.
units.literal: He began his career as acting aide in the light-chariot service of Liang's Heir of Linchuan, and was promoted in succession to water-and-arms clerk in the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, Pacifier of the West.

units.zh: 光大中，以公事免，尋起為通直散騎常侍。
units.en: In the Guangda era (567) he was dismissed on official grounds, then soon restored as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
units.literal: In the Guangda era he was removed for public business; soon he was raised again as Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 十二年，坐疆埸交通抵罪。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was punished for illicit dealings on the border.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was punished for trafficking at the frontier.

units.zh: 禎明元年卒官，時年七十二。
units.en: In the first year of Zhenming (587) he died in office, aged seventy-two.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he died in office, aged seventy-two.

units.zh: 又巧思過人，為起部尚書，軍國器械，多所創立。
units.en: His ingenuity surpassed others. As minister for founding works he devised much of the army's and state's equipment.
units.literal: He was also surpassing in ingenious thought; as Minister for Founding Works he created many of the army's and state's engines and gear.

units.zh: 時興皇寺朗法師該通釋典，〔八〕瑒每造講筵，時有抗論，法侶莫不傾心。
units.en: Master Lang of Xinghuang Temple had mastered the Buddhist canon. [8] Whenever Yang came to the lecture hall they argued points, and the monastic community hung on his words.
units.literal: At that time Master Lang of Xinghuang Temple had thoroughly mastered the Buddhist canon, and whenever Yang came to the lecture seat there was debate; the community of the Law all turned their hearts to him.

units.zh: 及王琳入寇，以瑒為使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢荊巴武湘五州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史，總留府之任。
units.en: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Ying, with full charge of the rear headquarters.
units.literal: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, Pacifying-the-West General, and Inspector of Ying, with overall charge of the rear headquarters.

units.zh: 周遣大將史寧率眾四萬，乘虛奄至，瑒助防張世貴舉外城以應之〔四〕，所失軍民男女三千餘口。
units.en: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning with forty thousand men in a sudden rush. Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi Gui opened the outer city to them. [4] More than three thousand soldiers and civilians, men and women, were lost.
units.literal: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning at the head of forty thousand men, who came by surprise in force; Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi Gui raised the outer city to welcome them, and there were lost among soldiers and people, men and women, more than three thousand persons.

units.zh: 時瑒兵不滿千人，乘城拒守，瑒親自撫巡，行酒賦食，士卒皆為之用命。
units.en: Yang had fewer than a thousand men. He held the walls himself, walking the battlements with wine and food. Every soldier fought for him to the last.
units.literal: At that time Yang's troops were fewer than a thousand; he manned the walls to resist; Yang personally went about encouraging them, walking the ramparts with wine and food; the soldiers all fought to the death for him.

units.zh: 周人苦攻不能克，乃矯授瑒柱國、郢州刺史，封萬戶郡公。
units.en: The Zhou attacked hard and failed. They then falsely invested him as pillar of state, inspector of Ying, and duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery.
units.literal: The Zhou men attacked bitterly and could not overcome him; they then falsely invested him as Pillar of State, Inspector of Ying, and Duke of a Ten-Thousand-Household Commandery.

units.zh: 及聞大軍敗王琳，乘勝而進，周兵乃解。
units.en: When word came that the main army had broken Wang Lin and was marching in triumph, the Zhou lifted the siege.
units.literal: When he heard the great army had defeated Wang Lin and was advancing in victory, the Zhou troops then lifted the siege.

units.zh: 瑒於是盡有中流之地，集其將士而謂之曰：「吾與王公陳力協義，同獎梁室，亦已勤矣。
units.en: Yang then held the entire mid-Yangzi. He assembled his officers and said: "We served the princes in righteousness and upheld Liang together. We have labored long enough.
units.literal: Yang then held all the midstream lands; he gathered his generals and said to them: "I and the princes exerted strength together in righteousness and jointly upheld the house of Liang—we have already toiled enough.

units.zh: 今時事如此，天可違乎！」
units.en: The times stand as they do. Who defies Heaven?"
units.literal: Now the times are thus—can Heaven be defied!"

units.zh: 遂遣使奉表詣闕。
units.en: He sent envoys with a memorial to court.
units.literal: He then sent envoys with a memorial to the court.

units.zh: 性通泰，有財物散之親友。
units.en: He was open-handed by nature and gave his wealth freely to kin and friends.
units.literal: By nature he was open and easy; he had wealth and goods and gave them away to kin and friends.

units.zh: 其自居處，頗失於奢豪，庭院穿築，極林泉之致，歌鍾舞女，當世罕儔，賓客填門，軒蓋不絕。
units.en: His own household leaned toward luxury: courtyards were terraced into gardens to the limit of woodland and spring beauty; singing bells and dancing girls were seldom matched in the age; guests packed his gate and fine carriages never stopped coming.
units.literal: In his own dwelling he rather failed in extravagance and pride; courtyards were dug through and built up to the utmost of forest and spring charm; singing bells and dancing girls were rare in the age; guests filled his gate and lofty carriages never ceased.

units.zh: 孫瑒有文武幹略、見知時主，及行軍用兵，師司馬之法，至於戰勝攻取，屢著勳庸，加以好施接物，士咸慕向。
units.en: Sun Yang had civil and military talent and won his sovereign's trust. In command he followed the marshal's art; in battle he took cities and won repeated glory. He was generous and approachable, and soldiers admired him.
units.literal: Sun Yang had civil and military capacity and plan, was known to the ruler of the age; in marching armies and using troops he followed the methods of the Marshal; as to defeating the enemy in battle and taking by assault, he repeatedly achieved merit and fame; moreover he loved giving and received people well—officers and men all admired and turned to him.

units.zh: 然性不循恆，頻以罪免，蓋亦陳湯之徒焉。
units.en: Yet he was not steady by nature and was often dismissed for fault—perhaps a man in Chen Tang's mold.
units.literal: Yet by nature he did not keep to constancy and was repeatedly removed for crimes—he was perhaps of Chen Tang's kind.

units.zh: 及卒，尚書令江總為其志銘，後主又題銘後四十字，遣左民尚書蔡徵宣敕就宅鐫之。
units.en: When he died, Secretariat Director Jiang Zong wrote his epitaph. The Last Emperor added forty characters of his own and sent Left Household Minister Cai Zheng with an edict to carve them at Yang's house.
units.literal: When he died, Secretariat Director Jiang Zong composed his funerary inscription; the Last Emperor also inscribed forty characters after the inscription and sent Left Household Minister Cai Zheng with an edict to his residence to carve it.

units.zh: 留異之反東陽，詔瑒督舟師進討。
units.en: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict put Yang in command of the river fleet to attack him.
units.literal: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict ordered Yang to command the river fleet in advance to campaign.

units.zh: 異平，遷鎮右將軍，常侍、鼓吹並如故。
units.en: After Yi was crushed he was made general who guards the right, retaining his attendant post and pipes and drums.
units.literal: When Yi was pacified he was transferred to General Who Guards the Right, regular attendant and martial pipes and drums unchanged.

units.zh: 〔三〕 徵瑒為太府卿 「太府卿」南史作「少府卿」，通鑑陳武帝永定三年同。
units.en: On "summoned Yang as minister of the grand storehouse": the Southern Dynasties history reads minister of the lesser storehouse; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.
units.literal: Summoned Yang as Minister of the Grand Storehouse—"Minister of the Grand Storehouse" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Minister of the Lesser Storehouse"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.

units.zh: 〔五〕 徵為散騎常侍中領軍 南史作「徵為侍中、領軍將軍」。
units.en: On "summoned as scattered cavalry regular attendant and central army commander": the Southern Dynasties history reads summoned as palace attendant and army commander.
units.literal: Summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander—the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "summoned as Palace Attendant and Army Commander."

units.zh: 〔六〕 領右軍將軍 「右」南史作「左」。
units.en: On "concurrently right army general": the Southern Dynasties history reads left for right.
units.literal: Concurrently Right Army General—"Right" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Left."

units.zh: 〔七〕 諡曰桓子 張森楷校勘記云「子」字衍。
units.en: On "posthumous title Huan-zi": Zhang Senkai's collation note holds that zi is superfluous.
units.literal: Posthumous title Huan-zi—Zhang Senkai's collation note says the character "zi" is redundant.

units.zh: 今按：瑒初封定襄縣侯，太建十二年坐疆埸交通抵罪免，後主嗣位，又復侯爵，此作「 子」不合，張說是。
units.en: Present review: Yang was first made marquis of Dingxiang; in Taijian year 12 he lost his title for frontier dealings; when Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—so writing "zi" here is wrong; Zhang is right.
units.literal: Present review: Yang was first enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county; in Taijian year 12 he was stripped for dealings at the frontier; when Emperor Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—writing "zi" here does not fit; Zhang is correct.

units.zh: 王出鎮郢州，瑒盡室隨府，甚被賞遇。
units.en: When the prince took up his post at Yingzhou, Yang brought his whole household to the headquarters and won high favor.
units.literal: When the prince went out to garrison Yingzhou, Yang moved his whole household with the headquarters and was greatly favored.

units.zh: 俄而侯景兵至，日夜攻圍，瑒督所部兵悉力拒戰，賊眾奔退。
units.en: Soon Hou Jing's troops came and besieged him day and night. Yang led his men in a full defense and drove the rebels back.
units.literal: Soon Hou Jing's troops arrived and attacked day and night; Yang supervised his command in full strength to resist; the rebel host broke and fled.

units.zh: 瑒偽許以緩之，而潛修戰具，樓雉器械，一朝嚴設，周人甚憚焉。
units.en: Yang feigned acceptance to buy time while secretly readying arms. Towers, parapets, and engines stood complete by morning, and the Zhou were deeply afraid.
units.literal: Yang pretended to agree to gain time, while secretly repairing war gear; towers, parapets, and engines were in one morning set in strict array; the Zhou men greatly feared him.

units.zh: 瑒懷不自安，乃固請入朝，徵為散騎常侍、中領軍。
units.en: Yang could not rest easy and begged to come to court. He was summoned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and central army commander.
units.literal: Yang was uneasy at heart and firmly asked to enter court; he was summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander.

units.zh: 〔五〕未拜，而世祖從容謂瑒曰：「昔朱買臣願為本郡，卿豈有意乎？」
units.en: [5] Before he took office, Emperor Wen said to him gently: "Zhu Maichen once longed to govern his home commandery. Do you feel the same?"
units.literal: Before he took the appointment, Emperor Wen spoke to Yang at ease and said: "Of old Zhu Maichen wished to be magistrate of his home commandery—do you have such a wish?"

units.zh: 高宗即位，以瑒功名素著，深委任焉。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yang's record and fame were already great, and the emperor relied on him heavily.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, because Yang's achievement and fame had long been outstanding, he deeply entrusted affairs to him.

units.zh: 瑒增脩城池，懷服邊遠，為鄰境所憚。
units.en: He strengthened walls and moats, won over distant peoples, and neighboring states feared him.
units.literal: Yang further repaired the walls and moats, won over the distant borders, and was feared by neighboring territories.

units.zh: 〔四〕 瑒助防張世（責）貴舉外城以應之 據通鑑陳文帝天嘉元年及元龜三九九改。
units.en: Note 4, on "Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shigui opened the outer city in response": emended from the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wendi, Tianjia year 1, and Yuan Gui 399.
units.literal: Note 4, on "Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shigui opened the outer city in response": emended according to the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wendi, Tianjia year 1, and Yuan Gui 399.

units.zh: 僕射徐勉、左率周舍、家令陸襄並同孝綽議。
units.en: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Intendant Lu Xiang all sided with Xiaochuo.
units.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Intendant Lu Xiang all agreed with Xiaochuo's deliberation.

units.zh: 陸家令止云『多歷年所』，恐非事證；
units.en: Lu the Household Intendant only cited 'many years'—I fear that is not proof;
units.literal: Household Intendant Lu only said 'for many years'—I fear this is not evidence of the matter;
